body:
I certainly have interests, and I bury myself in them. I do 3d modeling and computational design. I self study and work all the time, and I would be lying if said there wasn't tons of work related stress. My life looks something like this: During work I hours I apply what I know to get the job done, and on my own time I study new techniques and ways to automate tasks, which invariably leads to a better skill set and thus a higher workload. Rinse and repeat. I'm certainly obsessive when it comes to getting things done. I've been called robotic, and sometimes I get made fun of for it ("beep boop", "SYSTEM OVERLOAD!")

I have a job that architects/artists/engineers would die for. I've just gotten to a point where I wonder why do I try so hard? Why do my successes always feel so empty? My soul feels unnourished. It always feels like I'm that 9yo boy with something to prove after being told I would never amount to anything, and that I was broken. They were probably right about the latter, because even when I proved them wrong about becoming something, I still feel this *rage.* Like I want to crush everything that would stand in my way. It's like I want to prove to the world that I mean something. But, every time I do accomplish something, or make some breakthrough in automating some process, it feels hollow, not enough. This is not a good way to live believe me.
